column2: This too is a nine-syllable mantra; its worship is as before: the dative, the word "Rama", then the heart, like the five-syllable one.
Its sage, meditation and worship are all told like the six-syllable one. After "Rama", "Chandra" and "Bhadra" in the dative, and "pavakavallabha" (svaha):
two mantras are declared; the sage and worship as before. Fire, with the remainder, crowned with the moon:
the one-syllable mantra of the Lord of the Raghus is another wish-granting tree. Brahma is the sage, Gayatri the metre, Rama its deity.
With the mantra rich in six long vowels he should perform the six limbs. On the bank of the Sarayu, on a dais of coral trees, on a lotus seat:
he should contemplate Rama dark, seated in the hero's posture, shining with the knowledge-mudra, his hand resting on his left thigh, with Sita and Lakshmana.
Looking at the Self, of immeasurable splendour like Love, clear as pure crystal, solely from desire for liberation,
he should contemplate the Supreme Self and chant the mantra for six lakhs. All the rest — offering, daily worship and so on — is like the six-syllable.
A two-syllable mantra: "fire, with the seat of the remainder" — as in the one-syllable one, the sage, meditation, worship and so on.
With Om, Rama, Rama, Anga-cha-astra seeds, a two-syllable one; a three-syllable king of mantras: sixfold, giving all desires.
A two-syllable one ending in Chandra-Bhadra; twofold, four-syllabled; their sage, meditation and worship as with the one-syllable.
Om, Rama in the dative, armour, weapon, Agnipriya: this eight-syllable great mantra, its sage, worship and so on like the six-syllable.
Om, Maya, "Ramaya" at the end of the heart, ending in Om: this eight-syllable Shiva-Uma-Rama mantra gives all success.
Its sage is declared Sadashiva, its metre Gayatri; the deity here is declared Shiva-Uma-Ramachandra.
Having made the six limbs with the six-power..., the five Om syllables, he should meditate in the heart on the one worshipped by the gods:
We worship Rama, three-eyed, bearing a half-moon, trident-bearer, the best, whose whole body is dusted with ash, the matted-haired.
He should meditate on Uma, charming through Rama, the limit of beauty, crowned with the moon, three-eyed, bearing noose, goad, bow and arrow.
Having meditated thus, he should chant a hundred thousand and offer with three sweet things, with bilva leaves, fruits, flowers, sesame or lotuses.
Treasures and successes desired by the gods come of themselves. Om, Maya, and the elder brother of Bharata, Rama, Manobhava (Kama):
with "agnijaya": a twelve-syllable mantra, another wish-granting tree. Its sage is Angiras, the metre Gayatri, the deity again:
Shri Rama; the seed is Bhuvana; the power is Svaha. With the moon-one-sage-earth-eye syllables the limbs are conceived.
Meditation, worship and so on all should be done like the six-syllable. Om, heart, "Sitapate", "Rama" in the dative,
hana hana twice, armour, weapon: a sixteen-syllable mantra. Its sage is Agastya; its metre Brihati; the deity again:
Shri Rama; the seed "aham"; the power "ram". With the syllables Rama-sea-fire-Veda-eye the five limbs are conceived.
Meditation, worship and so on are all as with the six-syllable. Om and the heart, he should say "brahmanyasevyaya",
Ramaya akunthashabdanta, "tejase", "uttamashlokadhuryaya", "sva" (own), Bhrigu with Kamika,
dandarpitam priye: this mantra is held as the "Rama-Rama" syllable-mantra; its sage is Shukra, metre Anushtubh; its deity Rama.
He should make the five limbs with the feet and all; the rest like the six-syllable. A hundred thousand chants with a tenth part offering with milk-rice by the wise one.
For the one whose mantra is perfected there is enjoyment, liberation, and destruction of sins. At the start, "Dasharathaya", at the end he should say "vidmahe";
then he should say "Sitavallabhaya dhimahi"; "Tan no Ramah prachodayat" and the rest he should recite.
This Rama Gayatri is declared as granting the fruit of all desires. "Padma Sita" in the dative with two "tha" — a six-syllable one:
the sage is Valmiki, metre Gayatri; the deity again Sita Bhagavati; the seed "Shrim", Vahnisundari (svaha);
the power; with the seed rich in six long vowels he should conceive the limbs. Then he should meditate on the great goddess Sita, worshipped by the three worlds,
bright as heated gold, holding a pair of lotuses in two hands, her divine body shining with fine jewels and ornaments, auspicious in nature,
in varied clothes, moon-faced, lotus-eyed, joyful in heart, looking at the holy Raghava, mistress of the six qualities, seated at his side.
Having meditated thus, the mantra-knower should chant a hundred thousand, offer a tenth part with open lotuses and worship on the seat stated before.
Conceiving the form from the root, invoking Janaki in it, having worshipped, he should worship Rama on the right and Hanuman in front,
Lakshmana behind, the limbs in the six corners, the chief mantras on the petals, and the guardians of the world outside.
Having worshipped Vajra and the rest, he becomes lord of all success. With jasmine flowers smeared with sandal he should offer for subjugating a king;
with lotuses, wealth and grain; with blue lotuses, subduing the world; with bilva leaves, for gaining Lakshmi; with durva, for peace from fear.
What more need be said? By worshipping Sita one obtains good fortune, sons, grandsons, supreme happiness, wealth, grain and liberation.
Shakra, moon, "Lakshmanaya", the heart — a seven-syllable mantra. Its sage is Agastya, metre Gayatri; the deity again:
the great hero called Lakshmana; the heart is the seed and power. With the seed rich in six long vowels he should perform the six limbs.
He should meditate on the two-armed, gold-bright-bodied, lotus-eyed one, holding bow and arrow, his mind absorbed in service to Rama.
Having meditated thus, he should chant a hundred thousand and offer a tenth part with honey-mixed milk-rice, and worship on Rama's seat.
His worship is like Rama's; this gives all success. If a man wishes completeness of worship of Rama, he must definitely
with effort and respect worship Lakshmana. There are many forms of Shri Ramachandra giving success;
their practitioners should always do the auspicious worship of Lakshmana. A thousand and eight, or a hundred, by the attentive,
the mantra of Lakshmana is to be chanted by seekers of liberation, unwearied. Those who chant Rama mantras without chanting Lakshmana's mantra
do not succeed; there is loss at every step. He who constantly chants Lakshmana's mantra, devoted to solitude,
is freed from all sins and obtains all desires. This mantra, principally for victory, is the one means to regain a kingdom.
To regain a lost kingdom one should chant the mantra a hundred thousand, attentive; soon he regains his lost kingdom, without doubt.
Meditating on Rama in Ayodhya consecrated, with undistracted mind, having chanted the mantra fifty thousand times he regains a lost kingdom.
Meditating with respect on Lakshmana freed from the serpent-noose, chanting the mantra ten thousand times, he is surely freed from fetters.
Meditating on him relieved of pain by the herbs brought by Hanuman, chanting a hundred thousand, he surely conquers early death.
Meditating on him killing Meghanada, chanting the mantra a hundred thousand, he swiftly conquers even a great invincible enemy host.
Meditating on him intent on cutting off Shurpanakha's nose, chanting a thousand, he would conquer Indra and the others.
Remembering him making effort to serve Rama's lotus feet, chanting a hundred thousand in solitude, he is freed from a great disease.
For three months, controlling food, chanting daily seven thousand, with hundred-and-eight flawless hundred-petalled flowers,
having worshipped by rule and offered milk-rice with sugar, he chants the mantra and is freed from leprosy.
In solitude, controlling food, for six months by this rule he is freed from consumption, true, true, without doubt.
Reciting the mantra thrice over water in the morning, attentive, or at the three twilights, he should drink it daily: he is freed from all diseases.
Poverty is overcome; he becomes like Kubera; contact with poison and other faults never occurs.
He should daily wash his face with water consecrated by the mantra; he conquers terrible diseases arising in the mouth, eyes and so on.
Having drunk the consecrated water he surely conquers belly diseases. Having made an image of Lakshmana, he should give it with devotion by rule;
he is freed from all diseases, without doubt. One wishing for a bride, his mind set on taking a pure girl's hand,
meditating, should chant a hundred thousand, and offer a tenth with lotuses; he soon gains the desired girl, without doubt.
Initiated, firm in vows regarding the Jrimbhana weapons' mantras, meditating by rule he should chant the mantra daily for three months,
with worship first, seven thousand, master of senses; the man becomes knower of the truth of all sciences.
Meditating on him who did a wonderful feat at Vishvamitra's best sacrifice, chanting the mantra a hundred thousand, he is freed from great fear.
Having done his daily rites, pure, he should chant the mantra at the three times; freed from all sins he goes to Vishnu's supreme abode.
The initiated mantra-knower, free of stain by qualities, restrained in his own conduct, self-controlled, a householder, master of senses,
he who worships the Lord without regard to worldly fruit, free of desire, having burned up the masses of merit and sin, pure in mind,
free from return, attains the eternal state. One with desire, having obtained his wishes and enjoyed pleasures in mind,
and been immortal for long, goes to Vishnu's supreme abode. "Nidra-chandra", then for Bharata, ending in the heart:
the seven-syllable mantra; its sage and worship are as before. "Baka" with moon, the Shatrughna-para in the dative, ending in the heart:
this seven-syllable Shatrughna mantra gives success in all desires.
surrounded by great heroes such as Angada, Rudra-formed: "Stand, stand in the battle, wicked one," emitting a fierce sound...
Having worshipped him in Shiva-form and meditated, he should chant the mantra a hundred thousand, and offer a tenth part with rice mixed with milk, curd and ghee.
On the Vaishnava seat stated before, with Vimala and the others, conceiving the form from the root, worship of Hanuman should be done.
Success comes to men even by meditation alone, without doubt. Now I shall tell its practice out of desire for the good of people.
The practice of Hanuman is holy, destroying great sins; it is the most secret in the world, the supreme quick-success-giver,
by whose grace the practitioner would become conqueror of the three worlds. In the morning, having bathed on a river bank, seated on a kusha seat,
he should do pranayama and the six limbs, all with the root mantra. Having offered eight handfuls of flowers and meditated on Rama with Sita,
he should draw on a copper plate an eight-petalled lotus with filaments, with ground bad-sandal paste by a stick.
In the pericarp he should write the mantra, invoke the Lord of monkeys there, conceive the form with the root, and after meditation offer foot-water and the rest.
Having offered all perfumes and flowers with the root mantra, he should worship the six limbs on the filaments and then on the petals:
Sugriva, Lakshmana, Angada, Nala and Nila, Jambavan, Kumuda, Kesarin on the petals.
Then he should worship the guardians of the directions and Vajra and the rest. When the mantra is perfected, the mantra-knower accomplishes his own desire.
On a riverbank, in a forest, on a mountain or in a lonely place, the best practitioner should practise, having first taken possession of the ground,
controlling food, breath, speech and senses, having done the binding of directions and so on, preceded by placing and meditation.
He should chant a hundred thousand of the king of mantras, having worshipped as before. When the day of the hundred-thousandth comes, he should perform great worship.
With one-pointed mind, meditating well on the son of the Wind, he should chant day and night until the vision comes.
Knowing the practitioner to be firm, at midnight the son of the Wind, well pleased, goes before the practitioner,
and, giving the practitioner the desired boon, the Lord of monkeys departs. Having got the boon, the best of practitioners enjoys happiness of himself.
This holy practice has been revealed out of desire for the good of people, a secret hard to get even for the gods.
He should also accomplish other applications beneficial to himself. After the pair "moon and sky", in the dative: Pavananandana (Hanuman):
Vahnipriya at the end: this ten-syllable mantra gives all desires. The sage and the rest are as before; the six limbs too.
He should meditate on Hanuman in battle, bright as ten million suns, running to conquer Ravana, rising swiftly on seeing,
the great hero Lakshmana fallen on the battlefield, and having roused anger in the teacher, to seize the mountain,
shaking the three worlds with his shouts and boasts, proclaiming to the cosmic egg, having made his body terrible.
He should chant a hundred thousand and offer a tenth by the wise as before. Worship as before is declared by rule for this mantra.
When the mantra is so perfected, the mantra-knower should accomplish what is good for himself. There is also a secret practice of this best of mantras,
to be well hidden in all tantras and not given to just anyone. Rising in the Brahma-muhurta, having done daily rites, pure,
having gone to a river and bathed, invoking the holy place eightfold, then chanting the root mantra, he should sprinkle with the number of the suns (twelve).
Having thus done bathing and so on, on the Ganga bank or on a mountain or in a forest, having first taken possession of the ground,
inhalation is with the first syllables, retention with the five classes, and exhalation again with "ya" and others. Thus controlling the breath,
having done purification of the elements and so on up to the placing on the seat, then having meditated by the rule stated before and worshipped the Lord of monkeys,
before him the practitioner should chant ten thousand daily with respect. On the seventh day, he should perform great worship.
With one-pointed mind the mantra-knower should chant the mantra day and night. Having given great fear, in the remaining third part...
surely in the nights the son of the Wind comes; the Lord of monkeys gives the practitioner the boon as desired,
learning, wealth, kingdom or victory over enemies; he obtains it that very moment, true, true, without doubt.
Having enjoyed all desires in this world, at the end he attains liberation. "Sadyachitam vayuyugmam Hanumanta" he should say.
(A mantra in coded syllables: "phalanta, phakriya, netrayukta, kamika, then dhagga, dhagita, ayurasva...")
(The garuda-red mantra, with weapons-arrows-eyes syllables; the sage and the rest as before; Hari removes disease of the spleen.)
The deity is declared; on a belly with an enlarged spleen, a betel leaf is placed and covered above,
and eightfold cloth; then the best of practitioners, placing a split of bamboo on it, should let go and remember the Monkey.
He should heat a stick of wild hemp in a fire, a stick from a jujube tree, with this mantra seven times;
with it he should strike the bamboo-split on the belly seven times; the spleen disease surely perishes.
Om, "namo Bhagavate Anjaneyaya", then he should say "of so-and-so's fetters break, break", twice,
bandhamoksham kuru kuru svaha — this is held the mantra. Ishvara is its sage; the metre Anushtubh; the deity again:
the fetter-breaker, glorious Hanuman, son of the Wind. "Ham" is the seed, two "tha" the power; the application is release from bondage.
He should make the limbs with the seed rich in six long vowels. He should meditate on Hari holding a mountain in the left hand, the enemy-splitting pure axe in the other,
golden-hued, with earrings. Having meditated thus, he should chant a hundred thousand and offer a tenth part with mango sprouts,
and worship as told by the wise. A man in a great prison should chant ten thousand;
soon he is freed from the prison, certainly happy. Now I shall tell its yantra, auspicious, giving release from bonds:
a six-cornered figure inside eight petals, with the object's name; in the six corners he should write "dhruva" in the dative and "Anjaneya";
on the eight petals he should write Om, "Vatu vatu"; with gorochana and saffron having written the best yantra,
holding it on the head he should chant ten thousand for release from bondage. Having written this yantra on clay, he should wipe it out
with the right hand daily in a circle, the mantra-knower; by doing so he is freed from a great prison.
Gagana, jvalana, sakshi, markata — the two; then "toya"; "shashe makare parimunchati munchati";
then "shrinkhalikam" — a mantra of eight syllables, Veda-eye. Having written this mantra with the right hand and with the left
pushing it away, the wise one should chant the mantra a hundred and eight times; within three weeks, a prisoner is freed, without doubt.
The sage, worship and so on of this are done as before; a hundred thousand chants, a tenth part offered with auspicious substances.
On a fine cloth in the shape of a tail, with a razor-pen, he should draw with eight perfumes the beautiful form of the monkey king,
in its middle writing the eighteen-syllable mantra with the enemy's name. Binding it on the head, consecrated with the mantra, the king
conquers the entire host of enemies merely by sight, certainly. At eclipses of moon or sun and the like, he should have the above written on a banner;
taking the banner, the mantra-knower, from touching to releasing, should have the alphabet chanted, then offer a tenth;
with sesame mixed with mustard in a consecrated fire. Placing the banner on an elephant, the king should go to battle;
seeing the banner on the elephant the enemies surely flee. I shall tell the yantra of great protection of Hanuman:
he should draw an eight-petalled lotus with the pericarp holding the object's name; drawing an eight-cornered figure on the petals he should enclose it with the garland-mantra;
outside it enclosed with Maya, he should perform the infusing of life. Written with a gold pen on lovely birch-bark,
with Kashmiri saffron and gorochana, wrapped in three metals, the yantra accomplished by pouring should be worn on the arm or head.
In battle, in gambling, in dispute and lawsuit, he gains victory; he is not overcome by planets, obstacles, poisons, weapons or thieves.
Having removed all diseases, he lives long, a hundred years. With six long vowels, sky, fire and Om enclosing it:
an eight-syllable great mantra; now the Mala mantra is told. "Om Vajrakaya, Vajratunda" he should recite,
Kapila, Pingala, Urdhvakesha, Mahabala, Raktamukha, Tadijjihva, Maha...,
Raudradamshtrotkata, "kaha kaha", "karala", "by the great, firm blow, the killing of Ravana",
Vayu, Mahasetu, at the end of bandha, maha, "shailapravaha", "gaganechara", "ehi ehi" he should say,
Bhagavan Mahabala, at the end "parakrama"; "Bhairava ajnapaya ehi ehi", then "Maharaudra".
